title: Distill a teacher into a student: soft targets, the loss, and its gradient
brief: Soften a softmax with a temperature, write the distillation loss with its T-squared factor and its gradient, check the high-temperature logit-matching limit, add a feature-matching loss, and train a student on soft targets that beats the same student trained on hard labels.
hints: Divide the logits by T, subtract the row maximum, exponentiate, and divide by the row sum. For logits [6, 3, 0] and T = 3 you should get [0.6652, 0.2447, 0.0900].

KL(p || q) is sum(p * (log p - log q)). The teacher goes first: the loss is KL(teacher || student). With teacher [6, 3, 0], student [4, 3, 1], and T = 3, the soft term T^2 * KL is about 0.6633, and the hard cross-entropy for label 0 is about 0.3490.

The soft part of the gradient with respect to the student logits is T * (p_s^T - p_t^T): the KL gradient is (p_s^T - p_t^T) / T, and the T^2 factor turns it into T times the difference. The hard part is p_s - onehot(y). Divide the mix by n because the loss is a mean over rows.
As T grows, p^T is close to (1 + centred logit / T) / K. So T * (p_s^T - p_t^T) tends to (centred z_s - centred z_t) / K, where centred means the row mean is subtracted.
For the feature loss, let R = h_s @ P - h_t. The loss is sum(R^2) / (2 n) and the gradient in P is h_s.T @ R / n.
fit_student starts from W = 0 and repeats W -= lr * X.T @ distill_grad(X @ W, z_t, y, T, alpha). distill_grad already averages over rows, so do not divide by n again.
